lines.66: ## 10. HMPE creep at Rev A sustained load — named hard part [Likely — creep guidance is secondary-sourced (MP-001), spot-check pending]
lines.70: At SF 2.5 the HMPE bulk sections carry a steady centrifugal load of 28–40% of rated break strength (40% raw; 28% if the 30% strength derate is applied in sizing). Published HMPE guidance is to keep sustained load at or below ~20% of break for multi-year life (SK78 ≈ 8 years at 20% load, 20 °C). The centrifugal load is genuinely sustained in the rotating frame, so this is the unfavourable regime.
lines.72: **Consequence:** Reaching 20% sustained load would require SF ≈ 5, which cuts characteristic velocity by √2 and drives the 2.5 km/s reference mass ratio from ~41× to order ~800× under the Moravec form. That is a refutation of the design, not a variant of it. SF 2.5 therefore stands, and the creep exposure is carried as a named hard part rather than designed away.
lines.74: **Admissible outcomes (not yet decided):** (a) creep-governed tether replacement cadence, costed into ops; (b) hybrid material boundary shifted toward PBO for the high-stress fraction; (c) HMPE grade change — DM20-class is reported to creep >50× slower than SK78 (LR-001 §D), so grade may matter as much as geometry; (d) some mix of the above.
lines.76: **Evidence that would close or change this entry:** ST-002 coupon creep-rate ratio at ~20% vs ~40% of break (4–8 week hold); the TP-001 creep test series; a rope-maker application-engineering dataset on DM20 vs SK78 sustained-load life; a primary-source creep curve replacing the secondary guidance above.
